title: NYSHIP Mental Health Coverage for NY State Employees
desc: What NYSHIP and the Empire Plan typically cover for mental health — therapy, psychiatry, inpatient and outpatient care for NY State employees. Call 213-321-6518.
bodyHtml:
Mental health and addiction are deeply connected, and your NYSHIP benefits are built to cover both. If you are a New York State or local government employee, your plan typically includes meaningful behavioral health coverage — for therapy, psychiatry, and higher levels of care when you need them. This guide explains, in plain language, what NYSHIP mental health coverage usually includes and how to confirm your exact benefits. It is general information, not medical advice.

Federal parity protects your mental health benefits

Under the federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA), health plans that cover mental health and substance use treatment must do so on terms no more restrictive than they apply to physical health care. In practice, that means your NYSHIP or Empire Plan behavioral health benefits cannot carry harsher limits, higher copays, or tighter visit caps than comparable medical benefits. New York also has its own strong mental health coverage protections. If you believe a behavioral health claim has been improperly denied or subjected to more restrictive terms than a comparable medical benefit, you have the right to file an appeal — and in some cases, to request an external independent review.

What NYSHIP mental health coverage typically includes

Outpatient Therapy

Individual, group, and family counseling with licensed therapists, typically covered with a copay or coinsurance.

Psychiatry & Medication

Psychiatric evaluation and medication management for conditions such as depression, anxiety, and PTSD.

Intensive Outpatient & PHP

Structured day or evening programs for people who need more support than weekly therapy.

Inpatient & Crisis Care

Hospital-level mental health care for acute situations, typically covered when medically necessary.

Mental health and addiction together: dual diagnosis

Many people living with a substance use disorder are also coping with an underlying mental health condition — depression, anxiety, trauma, or PTSD. Treating only one rarely works. Integrated dual diagnosis treatment addresses both at the same time, and it is typically covered under the same behavioral health benefit. If you are not sure whether what you are facing is "mental health" or "addiction," that is exactly the kind of question a confidential assessment can help answer.

Your privacy is protected

Behavioral health records receive strong legal protection. Substance use disorder records carry extra confidentiality under federal law (42 CFR Part 2), and all of your health information is protected under HIPAA. Your employer is not told the specific care you receive through your NYSHIP plan.

How to confirm your mental health benefits

Every plan is a little different, and the only way to know your exact coverage — copays, any authorization requirements, and which providers are in network — is to verify. We do that for you at no cost and in confidence: we contact your plan's behavioral health administrator, confirm your benefits, and report back, usually within a few hours. You can also explore our NYSHIP rehab coverage guide or start a free coverage verification.

Page last reviewed August 2026 by the NYSHIP Detox Editorial Team.

If you or someone you love is in crisis, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline anytime — it is free, confidential, and available 24/7.

faq.q: Does NYSHIP cover mental health therapy?
faq.a: Yes. NYSHIP and the Empire Plan typically cover outpatient mental health therapy — individual, group, and family counseling — usually with a copay or coinsurance. Your exact cost and any visit limits depend on your specific plan, which we can verify for free.

faq.q: Does NYSHIP cover psychiatry and medication for depression or anxiety?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. Psychiatric evaluation and medication management are typically covered behavioral health benefits. Coverage specifics vary by plan, so it is worth verifying your benefits before your first appointment.

faq.q: Is mental health treatment confidential for state employees?
faq.a: Yes. Your treatment is protected under HIPAA, and substance use records have extra protection under 42 CFR Part 2. Your employer does not receive details about the specific care you use through your NYSHIP plan.

faq.q: Does NYSHIP cover treatment for both addiction and mental health at once?
faq.a: Yes. Integrated dual diagnosis treatment addresses a substance use disorder and a co-occurring mental health condition together, and it is typically covered under your behavioral health benefit.

faq.q: How do I find out exactly what my plan covers?
faq.a: The easiest way is to let us verify it for you at no cost. We contact your plan's behavioral health administrator, confirm your benefits and any requirements, and report back — usually within a few hours. Call 213-321-6518.

title: Empire Plan vs. NYSHIP HMO: Which Covers Rehab?
desc: Empire Plan vs. NYSHIP HMO plans for addiction treatment — how networks, referrals and authorization differ, and how to choose. Free check: call 213-321-6518.
h1: Empire Plan vs. NYSHIP HMO Plans: Rehab Coverage Compared
bodyHtml:
When you enroll in NYSHIP, you generally choose between The Empire Plan and a NYSHIP HMO. Both are required to cover addiction and mental health treatment, but they work differently — in how you access care, which providers are in network, and what approvals are needed. This guide compares the two so you can understand your options. It is general information, not insurance or medical advice; your exact benefits depend on your plan and region.

The Empire Plan in brief

The Empire Plan is NYSHIP's flagship plan and the choice of many New York State and participating local government employees. It tends to offer broad, statewide access to providers and generally does not require you to choose a primary care "gatekeeper" or get referrals to see specialists. Its behavioral health benefits — covering detox, inpatient and outpatient addiction treatment, and mental health care — are administered through a managed behavioral health program. Learn more on our Empire Plan rehab coverage page.

NYSHIP HMOs in brief

Depending on where you live and work, NYSHIP also offers regional HMO options — plans such as CDPHP, MVP Health Care, Excellus BlueCross BlueShield, and EmblemHealth. HMOs typically use a more defined local network and may ask you to coordinate care through a primary care physician and obtain referrals or prior authorization for certain services. In exchange, in-network costs can be predictable.

How they compare for addiction treatment

Network

Empire Plan: broad, statewide. HMO: a defined regional network — care is usually steered to in-network providers.

Referrals

Empire Plan: generally no referral needed. HMO: may require referral or care coordination through a PCP.

Authorization

Both may require prior authorization for higher levels of care such as residential treatment; the process differs by plan.

Out-of-Network

Empire Plan often has out-of-network benefits; HMOs typically cover little or nothing out of network except emergencies.

What's the same: both must cover treatment

Whichever you have, federal parity law (MHPAEA) requires your plan to cover substance use and mental health treatment on terms no more restrictive than medical care. Both the Empire Plan and NYSHIP HMOs cover medically necessary detox, inpatient/residential rehab, partial hospitalization, intensive outpatient, and medication-assisted treatment — the details (copays, authorization steps, network) are what differ. For the full picture, see does NYSHIP cover rehab?

Which is better for getting into treatment?

There is no single right answer — it depends on your region, your providers, and your situation. The Empire Plan's broad network and out-of-network benefits can make it easier to access a specific program, while an HMO can offer lower, more predictable in-network costs. What matters most is knowing exactly how your particular plan handles addiction treatment before you start. We verify that for you at no cost — including any referral or authorization steps — and report back, usually within a few hours. Start a free coverage verification or call 213-321-6518.

faq.q: Is the Empire Plan or a NYSHIP HMO better for rehab?
faq.a: Neither is universally better. The Empire Plan offers broad statewide access and usually no referrals, while HMOs offer a defined local network with potentially lower in-network costs. The best choice depends on your region and providers. Both must cover addiction treatment under parity law.

faq.q: Do NYSHIP HMOs cover the same addiction treatment as the Empire Plan?
faq.a: Yes — both are required to cover medically necessary detox, inpatient and outpatient rehab, and medication-assisted treatment. What differs is the network, referral rules, and authorization process, not whether treatment is covered.

faq.q: Do I need a referral for rehab on a NYSHIP HMO?
faq.a: Sometimes. HMOs may require you to coordinate care through a primary care physician or obtain a referral or prior authorization for certain services. We can confirm exactly what your plan requires when we verify your benefits.

faq.q: Does the Empire Plan cover out-of-network rehab?
faq.a: The Empire Plan often includes out-of-network benefits, though your share of the cost is usually higher than in network. HMOs typically cover little or nothing out of network except emergencies.

faq.q: Can I find out how my plan handles rehab before I commit?
faq.a: Yes, and you should. We verify your exact NYSHIP or Empire Plan benefits — including network, referral, and authorization steps — at no cost and in confidence, and report back, usually within a few hours. Call 213-321-6518.
